77.canonical: Treat variable, parameter, and return type annotations as readability hints only: they are ignored at runtime and never prevent assigning or passing a value of a different type, so do not rely on them for enforcement or safety.

84.canonical: Because plain assignment is a statement, not an expression, use the walrus assignment expression := (wrapped in parentheses) to combine evaluation and assignment, typically inside an if or while test.

95.canonical: Return multiple values by packing them into a tuple the caller unpacks (or a NamedTuple when access by named attribute also aids readability), and return None when there is nothing to return.

104.canonical: Treat a single leading underscore as a non-enforced convention marking a name as internal/protected (Python has no real data hiding, and a subclass may still use it), and a double leading underscore as triggering name mangling to _Classname__name; do not overthink privacy beyond this.
